title: Elazar ben Pe’irah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says that his name remained an everlasting disgrace and reproach: through him Yochanan the High Priest became a Sadducee and killed the sages of Israel. He cites [Kiddushin 66a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.66a.9-12): in the days of King Yannai (whom Hyman identifies here as Yochanan), the king had a friend, a scoffer, evil-hearted and worthless, named Elazar ben Pe’irah. Hyman identifies him with the Elazar ben Patora named in [Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 9:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.9.11.8), where Yehudah ben Pakhora is also named, “priests of…” [The supplied notice ends here.][^3]

notes.text: The supplied text ends with the incomplete כהני (“priests of…”). Its לא אוהב is also irregular; the translation reads the intended friend relationship without silently correcting the Hebrew. Hyman’s identification of Yannai with Yohanan is retained as his.
Hyman identifies Yannai with Yochanan and assigns responsibility for the killings to Elazar. The name forms Pe’irah, Patora and Pakhora reflect different witnesses.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, pp. 199–200) has היה לו אוהב, “he had a friend,” while the supplied Hebrew has לא אוהב. It continues after the cutoff with בעלי אגרופין. The linked Yerushalmi names Elazar ben Paḥora and Yehudah ben Pakhora in an account about taking portions by force. Hyman identifies Elazar with the figure in Kiddushin.
